symptom: An agent written with `create agent` (Agent Editor 2.2+) is refused at startup by ASU_AgentEditor: "Model with name  is referenced but could not be found for the Agent", and the refusal stops the import of every agent document. mx check and the build are green; MDL had no way to write the agent's selectedModel.
file: sdk/agenteditor/types.go and mdl/types/agenteditor.go (SelectedModel), agenteditor_read.go / mprread reader_documents.go, agenteditor_write.go (encoder, after model), agenteditor_carry.go (selectedModel modelled), visitor_agenteditor.go + visitor_strict_properties.go (SelectedModel, SelectedModelName), cmd_agenteditor_write.go + cmd_agenteditor_carry.go selectedModelFrom, cmd_agenteditor_alter.go (keys applied in sorted order), cmd_agenteditor_agents.go describe, validate_agent_selected_model.go (MDL-AGENT02). Tests: agenteditor_carry_test.go TestEncodeAgentContents_SelectedModel, cmd_agenteditor_selectedmodel_test.go, validate_agent_selected_model_test.go, visitor_agent_settings_test.go
cause: selectedModel {id, name} was carried on rewrite (#2037) but never modelled, so a new agent had none. AgentEditorCommons 2.2.1 and 2.6.0 AgentFromModel_Validate require SelectedModelID, and AgentFromModel_CreateUpdateAgent retrieves the DeployedModel where Model = SelectedModelID; IM_AgentFromModel maps only selectedModel/id (name is Studio Pro's display text). AgentEditorCommons 1.1.0 does not read it.
insight: **Read the importer, not the document, to learn what is required.** The stored documents showed selectedModel on one agent in five apps, which looked optional; the import mapping and the validation microflow (describe microflow AgentEditorCommons.AgentFromModel_Validate) showed it is mandatory from 2.2 and that only the id matters, which fixed both the syntax (id key, optional display name defaulting to the id) and the check rule's scope (every plain create agent, not only MxCloudGenAI). A key that is set by two alter assignments (id and name) must be applied in a fixed order: the Sets map iterates randomly, so the test sets both in one statement and the control (reverse order) fails. Controls: dropping the encoder field, leaving selectedModel unmodelled in the carry, ignoring the statement's SelectedModel, omitting it in describe and silencing MDL-AGENT02 each fail their test; a build without the encoder field changes GraphExplorer's unit on an ICXGraphPilot describe→exec round trip, where the fixed build changes none.
